short.q: Describe the texture of a typical Classical melody with accompaniment.
short.model: Homophonic: a clear melody on top, supported by accompaniment such as an Alberti bass, in balanced phrases.

short.q: Give two ways in which Romantic harmony differs from Classical harmony.
short.model: Romantic harmony uses more chromatic notes and dissonance, and modulates to distant keys; Classical harmony is simpler with clear cadences.
points: Modulations to remote keys, vs simple Classical chords

short.q: Why did the piano replace the harpsichord in the Classical period?
short.model: The piano can play gradually louder and softer by touch, which suits crescendo and diminuendo; the harpsichord cannot.

short.q: Explain what a concerto grosso is.
short.model: A Baroque piece in which a small group of soloists (the concertino) plays against the larger orchestra (ripieno), with continuo.

short.q: Name two ways Romantic composers made orchestras bigger and more colourful.
short.model: They added more brass (trombones, tuba), percussion, harp and extra wind such as piccolo or cor anglais, giving more timbres.
